sources.entry: Dev Browser by Sawyer Hood - A browser-automation plugin/skill that lets Claude Code drive a browser to test and verify its own work — full Playwright API plus pixel- and DOM-level computer-use toolsets, connecting to your running Chrome or a fresh Chromium. Notably secure and fast: scripts execute inside a QuickJS WASM sandbox with no host filesystem or network access, and a published benchmark s

summary.one_liner: dev-browser is a CLI, daemon, and Claude Code plugin that lets coding agents drive Chrome with short JavaScript scripts using the Puppeteer Page API, keeping the browser open between calls.
summary.what_it_does: The tool runs short JavaScript scripts against Chrome through a warm background daemon, so the browser and named pages persist across calls. Scripts get a browser object for listing, creating, and closing named or anonymous pages, plus Puppeteer Page objects. Pages gain extras: an accessibility-tree snapshot with stable element refs (such as e12) usable in Puppeteer selectors, a JPEG screenshot helper, and a waitForLoad helper and fill helper. It can launch an isolated Chrome profile or connect to an already-running browser via port, HTTP URL, WebSocket URL, or CDP socket. It also exposes an MCP server with run, pages, browsers, stop, and help tools. The README also covers a saveFile/readFile helper limited to a tmp directory and a benchmark script.
use_cases: let Claude Code verify its own web UI changes in a real browser
navigate a page once and inspect it across multiple agent steps
attach to a Chrome window I already have open
take screenshots of a running web app
run scripted browser checks from the terminal
give an AI agent a persistent browser through MCP
how_to_run: claude mcp add dev-browser -- dev-browser mcp --headless
notable: Scripts run in a fresh node:vm context per command with a warm daemon, giving ~13 ms empty-script latency per the README benchmarks
Accessibility-tree snapshots with stable element refs that work directly in Puppeteer selector calls
Can attach to a user's running Chrome or a remote CDP endpoint without closing it on idle timeout
Ships as a single release binary that bundles Bun and Puppeteer
Upgrading to 1.0 replaces the earlier Playwright/QuickJS implementation, with a migration command from doobie state
caveats: Windows and musl Linux are not supported; macOS and glibc Linux only
node:vm is explicitly stated not to be a security sandbox, and the README recommends permission allowlisting only where scripts are trusted
Snap-packaged Chromium on Ubuntu cannot read the default data directory; workaround is dev-browser install or DEV_BROWSER_CHROME
Computer-use helpers under page.cua and page.domCua are not part of 1.0; scripts from 0.2 need API changes
